transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Reed (Redwood SE), Sara Kim (BrightHealth), Liam O'Connor (BrightHealth), Priya Desai (BrightHealth), Amit Rao (BrightHealth)

Summary (auto): Quick sync on POC readiness and initial performance numbers. Confirmed missing pieces (VPC peering, KMS access), agreed to run a 24hr Dedicated benchmark and share next steps.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, uh, and we'll jump into the results from the short run we did last week.
[00:12] Sara: Hi Maya, I'm here, Sara, same for Liam, Priya, Amit are on.
[00:18] Liam: Yep here.
[00:22] Jonas: Great, thanks. I'll start with the infra notes, then Maya will go through pricing and next steps.
[00:30] Jonas: So infra first — we were able to confirm that the staging cluster can reach Redwood's staging endpoint over the peered VPC, but we hit an issue with the firewall rules on the right egress ports, so we couldn't complete the KV cache priming step.
[00:45] Amit: Yeah we noticed a bunch of 403s when the script tried to upload the prompt prefixes, so that matches.
[00:50] Jonas: Right. On the positive side, basic generation worked over hosted mode, and we saw latencies in the 160-250ms range depending on sequence length. The 95th percentile crept up to about 320ms on a bursty window — likely because batching fell back and caching missed prefixes.
[01:08] Sara: Do you think that's our network or something inside the Redwood runtime?
[01:12] Jonas: It's a mix. We saw some spikes correlated with larger payloads + cold KV cache. If KV prefix cache had the common prompts primed the 95th would be much closer to the median. Also batching config — our load pattern had short bursts so time-based batching could help.
[01:27] Maya: Can I ask for a quick clarification — when you say KV cache you mean the prefix/kvcache for the model runtime not the database cache, right?
[01:35] Amit: Yeah the KV cache used during autoregressive decoding, storing previous key/value states. There's some confusion in the logs because our infra team labeled a kubernetes config map kv-cache as well, so naming collided.
[01:45] Jonas: Exactly, naming collisions. The runtime's KV is in-memory per GPU. We recommended priming it with the top 200 prompts for your use case.
[01:55] Priya: On security, a couple of asks — KMS integration for encrypting model artifacts, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SSO/SAML for Redwood Console. Are those in scope for the POC?
[02:06] Maya: Yes those are standard asks. We can provide a checklist. We'll need your KMS ARN for the Dedicated test and an account role for log forwarding; Redwood supports syslog and S3-based delivery.
[02:18] Priya: Ok please send the checklist, and also the SOC2 stuff, we need evidence for procurement.
[02:24] Maya: We'll send the SOC2 package, note that for Private deployments we'd surface more artifacts but for Hosted/Dedicated we have the standard SOC2 Type II.
[02:34] Liam: Quick question about Dedicated vs Hosted — if we opt for Dedicated early, how fast can you spin up capacity for our benchmark?
[02:41] Jonas: We can provision a small Dedicated pool in 24-48 hours once peering and IP ranges are confirmed. For the benchmark we usually request a 2-4 hour load window plus a 24hr extended run if you want to look at sustained throughput and cache warmup.
[02:55] Maya: Pricing note — there's an hourly committed price for Dedicated and then usage on top if you burst. I'll share the spreadsheet after this call.
[03:04] Amit: About the prompts, we have a set of templated clinical summarization prompts. We'll send a sanitized sample. Any constraints on max tokens or attachments?
[03:14] Jonas: Token limits are configurable per model. For this POC we recommend keeping inference prompts under 2k tokens to avoid memory pressure; if you need longer contexts we can discuss chunking or KV strategies.
[03:26] Sara: We also want to test embeddings for semantic search — was that part of the current run?
[03:31] Jonas: Not yet, today's short run was purely generation. We can add an embedding pipeline to the benchmark; embeddings have different throughput/cost tradeoffs and usually use CPU or mixed inference paths.
[03:42] Maya: Ok for clarity let's put the immediate goals: get VPC peering + ports open so Jonas can run a 2hr benchmark, get sanitized prompt set from Amit, and get security docs to Priya.
[03:55] Priya: Also, can Redwood support bringing your own KMS in Dedicated? We need to control key material for compliance.
[04:03] Jonas: For Dedicated yes we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK). On Private installs we'd have full HSM/KMS options too.
[04:12] Liam: One small snag — our infra team needs the exact CIDR ranges Redwood will talk from for peering. Where do we find that?
[04:19] Maya: I'll include the IP ranges in the provisioning doc. We'll also put a short steps doc for peering.
[04:26] Sara: Perfect. Anything else on infra?
[04:30] Jonas: One more tuning note — batching parameters. For low-latency interactive flows you usually prefer very small batch sizes with immediate dispatch, but for throughput-oriented pipelines you increase batch and accept slightly higher p95. We saw that tradeoff in the mini-run.
[04:45] Amit: Could you share the exact config you used so we can replicate?
[04:50] Jonas: Yes, I'll push the load script to the shared drive and include the curl examples, and the recommended batching config.
[04:58] Maya: Moving to results summary — Maya here — baseline hosted run median 120-140ms, p95 320ms on burst windows. With primed cache and tuned batching we expect p95 to be under 220ms. Cost ballpark for hosted was around $0.02 per 1k tokens in the micro-run, Dedicated will drop unit costs but requires commit.
[05:20] Sara: Those numbers sound promising, can you quantify Dedicated savings?
[05:24] Maya: Roughly 30-50% unit cost reduction depending on utilization and quantization profile. We'll put scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[05:33] Priya: Any data residency notes? We need all logs and artifacts to stay in the EU region for certain workloads.
[05:40] Maya: We support region pinning for model endpoints and log storage. For Dedicated we'd provision in your selected cloud region. For Hosted endpoints we can pin to the EU region too — just note some third-party tooling might be US-based.
[05:55] Liam: Ok good. About the benchmark — what are the go/no-go success criteria again?
[06:00] Jonas: We proposed: functional correctness on 95% of prompts, p95 latency < 220ms for interactive flows after cache warmup, and sustained throughput target of X requests/sec for API paths — we'll finalize X once you provide target QPS.
[06:16] Sara: Our target is 80 QPS at 95% availability during peak, with average session length ~30 tokens.
[06:24] Jonas: Great, that'll inform pool sizing.
[06:28] Maya: Ok let's align on schedule — if Amit sends prompts by Friday (2026-05-07) and Liam confirms peering by Saturday (2026-05-09) Jonas can run the Dedicated benchmark early next week.
[06:41] Amit: I'll get the sanitized set over by EOD Friday.
[06:44] Liam: I'll prioritize peering, should be able to confirm ranges by Sat.
[06:48] Priya: I'll review SOC2 docs when you send them, and flag anything missing.
[06:52] Jonas: Quick note on tooling — we can instrument tracing to show per-token timing, and we'll provide the console dashboards with per-route latency and cost breakdowns so you can see where tokens go.
[07:03] Sara: That's helpful, especially to correlate user flows to cost.
[07:07] Maya: Any other blockers?
[07:10] Sara: Not from product side.
[07:12] Priya: One ask — can we get a short architecture diagram for Dedicated with peering and KMS flow? That helps our security review.
[07:20] Maya: Yes we'll include that in the security pack.
[07:24] Jonas: I'll also include an example of the KV cache priming script and the recommended batching params.
[07:30] Maya: Alright, recap of next steps and owners — I'll send pricing + IP ranges + SOC2 package; Jonas will push the load scripts and schedule the benchmark; Amit and Liam to complete prompts and peering; Priya to validate security checklist.
[07:48] Sara: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:51] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark window.

Notes/Links shared during call:
- Shared drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/bh-poc
- Pricing spreadsheet (to be attached): link in follow-up
- SOC2 package: will be shared privately (redwood.com/sec/soc2)

End of transcript.

Recap (auto): POC is ready to proceed once peering and KMS details are provided. Redwood to run Dedicated benchmark after access and prompts are in. Action items captured; next sync scheduled ad-hoc around benchmark window.
